named_confounds: one passage per work sampling noise
rationale: Each of the 6766 works has 1 passage. Rate = DISTANCE_TRAVEL count / n_passages per work. For each genre I averaged works equally, took late (year>=1876) minus early, then averaged the 8 genres equally. Estimate +0.0082. The 95% CI from a stratified bootstrap (5000 resamples within genre x period) is [-0.016, 0.031], which includes zero. Genre-level differences go both ways (adventure, juvenile and sensation are slightly lower late; historical, romance and collection are higher). Decade rates stay flat at about 0.10-0.12. Restricting to high-confidence dates gives +0.023, and a 1857-1895 window gives +0.011; neither is clearly different from zero. The early cells are small (38-264 works per genre), the label is binary per passage, and dates are uncertain, so noise could hide or fake a small change. The cited passages are examples of the construct only and do not show a trend. The data do not support a robust historical shift.
